scenes.voiceover: Your parents moved to America for you. They sit in your living room all day. But who is actually taking care of them?
scenes.image_prompt: Elderly Indian couple sitting alone in American suburban living room

scenes.voiceover: Indian Americans over sixty-five have doubled in a decade. Four point four million strong — and the safety net barely exists.
scenes.image_prompt: Data infographic showing 4.4M Indian Americans, seniors doubled 2010-2020

scenes.voiceover: Many arrived on dependent visas — no English, no Medicare, no Social Security. No one to talk to. That is not care. That is containment.
scenes.image_prompt: Elderly Indian woman alone watching Hindi TV in American living room

scenes.voiceover: In Queens, India Home serves fifteen hundred seniors a year — with meals, yoga, and an AI-powered food pantry stocked with dal and basmati rice.
scenes.image_prompt: South Asian seniors sharing meals and doing yoga at India Home community center in Queens

scenes.voiceover: Their children are the sandwich generation — torn between aging parents and growing kids, with cultural guilt pulling from every direction.
scenes.image_prompt: Split scene showing Indian-American professional at work and elderly parent waiting alone at home

scenes.voiceover: The first generation that made it to America is aging out. The question is whether we will build the answer before they leave the conversation entirely.
scenes.image_prompt: Elderly Indian hands held by younger hands with NYC skyline in golden hour background
